source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Lemma 13 defines eta-star as the minimum nonzero eigenvalue over R_X^M for M subseteq [n] and uses eta-star/n to preserve approximate ranks for every subset.
The paper studies score-based CRL under unknown linear and general transformations and states one stochastic hard intervention per node suffices for linear-transform identifiability.
The proceedings abstract states that a single intervention on each latent variable is sufficient for identifiability in the linear latent causal-model setting.
The proceedings says that “[79, Corollary 4.5]” details spectral-projector computation; [79] is the related arXiv full version, not a corollary numbered 4.5 in the proceedings itself.

Either anchor Theorem 2 to a named published singleton-output CRL workflow and show the weak-edge family defeats it, or move the generic no-return theorem to non-headline motivation.

Prove an explicit inclusion between the source paper's applicable Gaussian perfect-intervention subclass and the proposed transcript-local class, including all non-margin source side conditions, to make the strict improvement auditable rather than proof-method-specific.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Sobczyk version attribution and sharpen or demote the unanchored impossibility theorem; the positive transcript-local margin kernel can then proceed as a field-tier target.
